entities.name: Spike-free MEG localization
observations: Resting-state interictal MEG band-power abnormalities provided clinically useful localization in 32 refractory neocortical-epilepsy patients; strongest-abnormality resection predicted outcome with AUC 0.71 and combined MEG+iEEG model AUC 0.80.
This approach does not require visible interictal spikes, although the study did not establish performance in a strictly spike-absent subgroup.

entities.name: Resting-state network localization
observations: An E/MEG embedded Hidden Markov Model with connectivity and graph analysis localized the intracranial-EEG-defined seizure-onset zone in 6 of 10 seizure-free patients, with approximately 15 mm error; performance degraded with lower signal-to-noise ratio.
This supports feasibility but reflects small-sample, network-level validation rather than a high-sensitivity clinical test.

entities.name: Spike-independent network mapping
observations: In 37 surgical patients, MEG/EEG functional connectivity and hub centrality were informative in both spike-containing and spike-free data, correlated with intracranial EEG at Spearman rho 0.4–0.9, and predicted outcome with positive and negative predictive values at least 55%.
Network measures outperformed conventional spike dipoles for outcome prediction in that study.

entities.name: Clinical maturity limitation
observations: Resting-state interictal MEG can reveal abnormal spectral regions, pathological states, and connectivity hubs without visually obvious spikes, but evidence is mainly from small retrospective cohorts with heterogeneous methods and limited prospective validation.
These methods generally identify epileptic networks rather than uniquely separating seizure-onset tissue from propagation or nonessential abnormal cortex.
